newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 97 budget cuts deficit 50 trln lire - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Italy 97 budget cuts deficit 50 trln lire - Minister.

text.p: The 1997 budget will aim to cut 50 trillion lire off next year's deficit and will include a special Europe tax as well as savings in health and pensions spending, Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi said on Thursday.

The budget, which was originally expected to seek savings of 32.4 trillion lire next year, will be formally unveiled on Friday. Fantozzi was speaking to reporters after a summit of government allies chaired by Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
It was not immediately clear if the proposals had won the backing of the hard-left Communist Refoundation, which has staunchly opposed any cuts in sensitive welfare spending.

Prodi depends on Refoundation for a majority in the lower house of parliament but the media has speculated that the prime minister may be prepared to stake his government's survival on the need for a tougher budget package.
Fantozzi said the budget would seek savings of two trillion lire in health spending and a further two trillion lire of cuts in pensions.

The government wants to increase the weight of the budget in the face of weakening 1996 accounts and fears that without tough additional measures Italy will fall behind in its bid to be a founder member of the planned single European currency in 1999.
